sections.title: Definition & Purpose
sections.content: Perimetry measures the sensitivity of the retina to light stimuli across the visual field. It maps the 'island of vision in a sea of darkness'. Static perimetry (automated) assesses threshold at fixed locations, while kinetic perimetry moves stimuli from non-seeing to seeing areas.

sections.title: The SITA Revolution
content: SITA (Swedish Interactive Thresholding Algorithm): Uses mathematical models to predict thresholds.
SITA Fast: Reduces testing time by ~50% with minimal loss in sensitivity.
SITA Faster: Further reduces time, removes blind spot monitoring to optimize fixation.
SITA Faster 24-2C: Adds 10 peripheral points specifically to detect glaucomatous damage in the central 10 degrees.

sections.title: Red Flags in Reliability
content: False Negatives > 20%: Suggests fatigue or inattention.
Gaze Tracking Graph: Look for spikes, indicating frequent ocular movements.

sections.title: Clinical Workflow: The Perimetry Process
content: Step 1: Proper refraction for age and testing distance (add +3.25D for near for 30cm).
Step 2: Trial frame or bowl-mounted lens correction (prevent rim artifacts).
Step 3: Patient instruction and practice 'dummy' run.
Step 4: Real-time gaze monitoring during testing.
Step 5: Analysis of Global Indices (MD, PSD, VFI).

content.explanation: G (Global Indices: MD/PSD), L (Losses/Fixation), A (Artifacts: Rim/Ptosis), D (Defect morphology: Arcuate/Nasal Step).

sections.title: Landmark Studies
content: OHTS (Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study): Utilized SAP (Standard Automated Perimetry) to define conversion to glaucoma.
EMGT (Early Manifest Glaucoma Trial): Established the 'Mean Deviation' (MD) as a primary metric for progression.
Comparison Studies: Confirmed that SITA-Faster provides comparable clinical utility to SITA-Standard while increasing patient satisfaction.
